steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Social policy: government actions addressing social problems (education, welfare, crime, health). Sociology influences policy through evidence, evaluation and advocacy.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Evidence-based policy: using research evidence to design policies. Example: Sure Start was based on research showing early intervention improves outcomes. However, policies are also influenced by political ideology, economics and public opinion.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Positivist view: sociology should provide objective evidence for rational policymaking. Interpretivist view: sociology should give voice to lived experience to shape humane policy. Both contribute.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Value-free vs value-laden: Weber argued sociology should be objective, but values inevitably influence topic choice. Marx: the point is to change society. Modern view: complete value-freedom is impossible; transparency about values is essential.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Explain how sociological research can influence social policy, giving examples. | Compare positivist and interpretivist views on sociology and social policy. | Evaluate whether sociology should aim to influence social policy or remain value-free.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Sociology -> evidence -> policy. Examples: Beveridge, Macpherson, inequality research. Positivist = objective evidence. Interpretivist = lived experience. Both needed. Value-free = credibility. Value-laden = honesty. TRANSPARENCY about values is the key.
